about.remark: Currently available for freelance engagements and open to employment opportunities.

project-1.title: Forensic Case Management Framework & Tool Architecture

parts.content: Developed a digital forensics requirements framework and open-source case and evidence management tool architecture, addressing a market dominated by proprietary tools. Combined a comprehensive literature review and comparative tool analysis to design a secure-by-design microservice reference architecture that ensures chain-of-custody integrity and separates forensically sensitive evidence from operational data. Implemented a partial proof-of-concept prototype for limited usability testing.
takeaways: Conducted requirements analysis of open-source digital forensics case management.
Designed a theoretical requirements framework and practical forensic tool architecture.

parts.content: Identified a gap in open-source tooling for DF case and evidence management. The few existing tools are mostly proprietary and limited in accessibility and the topic is under-researched despite growing challenges for practitioners. Conducted a comprehensive literature review, derived a requirements framework and compared six existing tools against the framework. Subsequently, designed a modular microservice-based reference architecture and implemented a partial proof-of-concept prototype to enable limited usability testing.
takeaways: Addressed a gap in accessible open-source forensic case management tools.
Performed a lit review, gap analysis, requirements analysis and tool engineering.

parts.content: Analysed 22 academic sources and derived theoretical functional, operational and usability requirements, resulting in a DF case management reference framework with 8 modules. Compared 6 existing tools against the framework in a gap analysis and identified their gaps. Designed an open source, secure-by-design reference architecture that addresses these gaps and implements the framework in practice, with 16 microservices and 20 forensic and security properties covering chain of custody, trust boundaries, data isolation and audit logging. Built a partial proof-of-concept prototype with FastAPI, React, PostgreSQL (five database models), JavaScript, Python, REST APIs and WebSockets, fully containerised with Docker Compose, to evaluate technical feasibility and run limited usability testing. Documented the framework, architecture and evaluation in a journal paper (under review).
takeaways: Derived an 8-module requirements framework, followed by a gap analysis of 6 tools.
Designed an architecture with 16 microservices and 20 forensic & security properties.

parts.content: Delivered a DF case management requirements framework designed as a component checklist and gap identifier for tools. Designed a secure-by-design open source reference architecture as a blueprint for open-source tool implementations, featuring comprehensive forensic and security properties necessary for forensic soundness. Implemented a working prototype using a modern stack to validate its technical feasibility and usability. Gained hands-on experience in turning research-derived requirements into a microservice architecture and a full-stack implementation. Gained an understanding of forensic investigation workflows and forensic integrity techniques, including chain of custody, data isolation and audit logging. Contributed the work to the research community through a journal paper currently under review.
takeaways: Delivered a comparable requirements framework and open-source blueprint.
Learned about evidence handling, forensic soundness and investigation workflows.

parts.content: Designed and secured the foundation of a three-tier, Linux-based cybersecurity training server for university students. Participants first discover the exposed services, then work through guided exercises and finally attack real, live applications to find genuine vulnerabilities. Architecture, hardening, operating policies and documentation were completed and development of the first exercises began. The project was discontinued when its academic supervisor left the university and no successor took over.
takeaways: Designed a three-tier Linux training server for university students.
Hardened server with discoverable ports, guided exercises and live applications.

parts.content: The project aimed to provide students with a controlled environment to gain hands-on experience with real-world web application and infrastructure vulnerabilities while helping selected live applications identify and address security weaknesses. A hardened host with restricted access and isolated training environments was provided for network scanning, practising common vulnerabilities and attack techniques, featuring a defined process for responsibly disclosing findings.
takeaways: Students lacked secure environments for practicing web and infrastructure attacks.
Provided restricted host, isolated labs, vulnerability testing and responsible disclosure.

parts.content: Configured iptables to secure the server, closed non-essential ports and hardened SSH according to best practices. Implemented port knocking and tested access controls with Nmap and netcat. Enforced secure password policies, restricted root access and established a dedicated admin account for privilege separation. Created technical documentation covering server architecture, setup and operational procedures. Designed learning exercises based on OWASP Top 10 with instructional texts, explanations, featuring user accounts, passwords and hints for live applications. Developed practical challenges covering SQL injection, phishing via a dedicated email account, password cracking and injection and logic flaws using Burp Suite. Created policies to maintain live applications on their latest versions to expose students to new vulnerabilities and established a reporting process via a dedicated server email account, allowing only the first student to report each finding to prevent duplicate submissions.
takeaways: Hardened Linux server with firewall and access restrictions and verified with Nmap.
Designed OWASP-based exercises (SQL injection, phishing) and a reporting process.

parts.content: Delivered a secured and documented foundation for a university training lab encompassing server architecture, setup, operating policies and a responsible disclosure process, using a dedicated GitHub repository. The exercises were only started and the lab was never deployed. The project provided practical experience in Linux server hardening, network security and the design of controlled environments for hands-on cybersecurity training.
takeaways: Delivered documented server architecture, security policies and setup.
Gained practical experience in Linux hardening and network security.

parts.content: Supported GDPR compliance and web application security initiatives within a university environment, combining independent research into European and German data protection legislation with practical privacy assessments and collaborative security testing. Applied regulatory knowledge to assess personal data processing activities, identify compliance gaps and strengthen application security.
takeaways: Researched European and German data protection legislation.
Applied findings through privacy assessments and collaborative security testing.

parts.content: The university required greater visibility into personal data processing activities, potential GDPR compliance gaps and web application security risks. The scope encompassed an in-depth assessment of one university web application, including comprehensive documentation of PII data flows and processing activities, as well as a basic vulnerability assessment to identify potential security weaknesses and improve the application's overall data protection and security posture. In addition, an initial assessment of a second university web application was conducted.
takeaways: Addressed limited transparency in university data processing.
Conducted security & privacy assessment of two web applications.

parts.content: Independently researched the GDPR, BDSG, relevant legal terminology and additional European and national data protection legislation. Applied regulatory requirements to practical GDPR assessments, including data-flow mapping, PII identification, privacy risk evaluation and RoPA (Record of Processing Activities) documentation. Collaborated with a system administrator on scoped vulnerability assessments, jointly investigating, validating and reporting security findings, coordinating remediation efforts and regularly updating the supervising Data Protection Officer (DPO) on findings and progress.
takeaways: Mapped data flows, identified PII and documented privacy risks.
Conducted collaborative vulnerability assessments and coordinated with stakeholders.

parts.content: Assessed personal data processing across 11 functional areas and supported GDPR compliance through structured data-flow analysis and RoPA documentation. Collaboratively assessed two university web applications, identifying and responsibly reporting five validated vulnerabilities and coordinating risk-based remediation. Strengthened expertise in data protection legislation, privacy risk assessment and application security while developing practical skills in independent research, technical investigation, cross-functional collaboration, stakeholder communication and remediation coordination.
takeaways: Assessed 11 functional areas (5 vulnerabilities) and documented GDPR compliance.
Developed expertise in privacy risks, security and stakeholder coordination.

experience-3.title: Software Developer – Forensic Lab Equipment (Part-Time)
experience-3.type: Attestor Forensics GmbH, Bad Wurzach, GER

parts.content: Modernisation and functional extension of a legacy C# Windows desktop application (Windows Forms) for forensic hardware log analysis. The application processes hardware diagnostic and event logs containing operational measurements and environmental data, including parameters such as temperature and humidity relevant to forensic operations. The project focused on restructuring the legacy codebase, introducing a modular software architecture, extending log processing capabilities, implementing data transformation and localisation features and redesigning GUI components to improve data visualisation, interpretation and reporting.
takeaways: Modernised a legacy C# Windows Forms app for forensic log analysis.
Added modular architecture, extended functionality and improved GUI visualisation.

parts.content: The existing application lacked a defined software architecture, modular structure and technical documentation. Application logic, GUI functionality and data processing were combined within a small number of files, resulting in redundant code and limited maintainability. The application also required functional extensions to process additional log fields, correctly interpret measurement values and present operational data through the GUI. The scope covered codebase restructuring, separation of presentation and business logic, implementation of new processing and visualisation features, internationalisation and comprehensive technical documentation.
takeaways: The application lacked a clear architecture, modularity and maintainability.
Remodelled codebase and added features, visualisation and technical documentation.

parts.content: Analysed the legacy C# application and restructured it by creating a modular directory hierarchy, reorganising classes and functions by responsibility and separating GUI components from business logic. Removed redundant code and added new application functionality. Extended log processing to extract additional fields from hardware diagnostic and event logs, integrated the values into the GUI and tested their correct interpretation and display. Implemented measurement conversion functions, including temperature units, based on hardware engineering specifications. Redesigned GUI layouts and integrated diagrams, filters and custom data views according to sales requirements. Added multilingual support for international markets. Rebuilt the technical documentation from scratch, documenting individual classes and methods in an API-style format. Managed all source code changes with SVN.
takeaways: Introduced modularity, advanced log parsing and functional conversion features.
Improved GUI with visual elements and added new languages for enhanced usability.

parts.content: Transformed the unstructured legacy codebase into a modular C# application with separated GUI and business logic, making it maintainable and extensible. Extended log processing with additional diagnostic and event data, added measurement conversions, improved data visualisation through redesigned diagrams, filters and views and delivered multilingual support for international markets. Established the first technical documentation for classes and methods. Collaborated cross-functionally with hardware engineering and sales, consolidated their differing requirements, defined the final requirements and implemented them as application features. Strengthened skills in requirements engineering, stakeholder communication, independent prioritisation, legacy system modernisation, software architecture and forensic log processing.
takeaways: Modernised the codebase and enhanced features, visualisation and documentation.
Strengthened requirements engineering and cross-functional communication skills.

Broad-based IT education covering software and systems development, networking, operating systems and core computing concepts, with a focus on cybersecurity, digital forensics and data privacy. reference-1.body: I have known Blue since his enrolment on the MSc Ethical Hacking programme at Abertay in September 2024, when he took my Digital Forensics class. His approach to complex problems was mature, methodical and determined, underpinned by a genuine enthusiasm for the subject. It was therefore no surprise when Blue was awarded the NCR Atleos Prize for Best Student on the Programme. Beyond his academic strengths, Blue is thoughtful, reliable, engaging and easy to work with: a real asset to any team.

reference-2.body: Blue Butscher worked together in IT security and data protection related projects. Blue's contribution was highly valuable and useful: He provided great ideas and concepts, that he could very well argue for. His critical thinking skills supported by a good technical background made good judgement. He is able to do both: Good analysis of a status-quo as well as to develop ways to improve and augment any solution. While we worked together, Blue proved his curiosity in acquiring new knowledge and his ability to do so very fast. Blue is a trustworthy, reliable and highly committed team member. I therefore strongly recommend working with Blue.

reference-3.body: During his time as my student, he consistently demonstrated a strong work ethic, excellent attendance, and a genuine willingness to engage with both the course material and wider class discussions. He approached his studies with professionalism and maturity and contributed positively to the learning environment throughout. What particularly distinguished him from his peers was his attention to detail. He completed his work carefully and thoughtfully, often demonstrating a high level of precision. His commitment to producing sound work, combined with his enthusiasm for learning, made him a standout student.

reference-4.body: Blue consistently demonstrated reliability and professionalism. He was punctual, arrived prepared and ready to begin work. His self-directed approach meant he took initiative, managed tasks independently, and required minimal supervision. Blue also showed strong discipline and maintained steady progress on all assigned work. Overall, it was encouraging to see his commitment to producing quality work.
